text.en:
In Thanjavur, Hari stood in front of a temple tower so tall he had to bend his neck to see the top.
"King Rajaraja Chola built this a thousand years ago," said his grandmother.

The Cholas became very powerful. Rajaraja I built the Brihadisvara temple at Thanjavur. His son Rajendra I sent an army to the Ganga and built Gangaikonda Cholapuram. The Cholas also had a strong navy and traded with Southeast Asia.
Chola villages ran local assemblies. Inscriptions describe how members were chosen. Bronze statues of gods made in this period, like the Nataraja, are famous.
In the north the Chandelas built the Khajuraho temples. Mahmud of Ghazni raided northwestern India in the early 11th century. The scholar Al-Biruni wrote about India. In 1192 Muhammad of Ghor defeated Prithviraj Chauhan at the second Battle of Tarain.
Rajaraja Chola built the Brihadisvara temple at Thanjavur.
The Cholas had a strong navy and traded with Southeast Asia.
The Chandelas built the temples of Khajuraho.
In 1192 the second Battle of Tarain changed the politics of the north.

problem.en: How did the Chola navy help the kingdom?

text.en: A navy protects trade at sea.
It allowed expeditions across the sea.
So the Cholas grew rich and strong.

prompt.en: A friend says India was isolated in those days. How will you reply?

Al-Biruni came and wrote about India.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking India had no links abroad.

points.en: The Cholas built great temples and a strong navy.
Mahmud of Ghazni raided; Al-Biruni wrote about India; Tarain was fought in 1192.
